routes.label: Find the total white area and check uniqueness

question: Marla has a large white cube that has an edge of \(10\) feet. She also has enough green paint to cover \(300\) square feet. Marla uses all the paint to create a white square centered on each face, surrounded by a green border. What is the area of one of the white squares, in square feet?
solution:
Centering specifies where each white square is placed, but it does not require the six squares to have the same size.

Each cube face has area \(10\cdot10=100\) square feet, so the total surface area is \(6\cdot100=600\) square feet. Painting \(300\) square feet leaves
\[
600-300=300
\]
square feet white. Thus the average area of the six white squares is \(300\div6=50\) square feet.

However, individual areas can differ. For example, use centered \(6\)-by-\(6\) white squares on three faces and centered \(8\)-by-\(8\) white squares on the other three. They have positive green border widths of \(2\) feet and \(1\) foot, respectively. Their total white area is
\[
3\cdot36+3\cdot64=300,
\]
so the painted area is exactly \(600-300=300\) square feet. None of these white squares has area \(50\).

If we additionally assume that all six white squares have equal area, each has area \(300\div6=50\) square feet, choice \(\text{D}\). Without that assumption, the area of one white square is not uniquely determined.
